identity: Front matter plus the opening two dated entries of an Arabic translation of a German literary travel diary: Klaus Reichert, 'ayyam al-sahra' (Wuestentage / Desert Days), subtitled 'rihla' (a journey), translated by Dr. Dana Shaker, reviewed by Mustafa al-Sulaiman. Tokens 0-32 are title-page and colophon furniture: author, title, subtitle, translator credit, reviewer credit, half-title, the place header 'Nuweiba Sinai', the dateline '23 Kanun al-Awwal (December) 2005', and the locative header 'in the Gulf of Aqaba'. Tokens 33-611 are the diary proper in eleven paragraphs of first-person observational prose: the weather and the two shores of the gulf, with a cloud that looks first like a fish and then like a skeleton; the narrator's apprehension before the camel journey; the Bedouin Lafi and the saddling of the camel Thuban; Lafi's stone house, his wife Saliha, the tea and the afternoon prayer; the episode of the photographs of the narrator's friend and Saliha's reaction to them; the drive back in the pickup through a dust squall; a bare list of illness symptoms and a question about why he is here; then the second dateline (24 December 2005) and the loading of the three camels.
law: Register first (LAW 6). This is a TRANSLATED European literary diary, not an Arabic confessional memoir, so my doctrine's section H welding default does not apply: the translator is rendering Reichert's paratactic German full stops, and the sentence unit runs roughly 9-12 tokens. The operative rules I read off this text: (1) Asyndeton between two finite predications is the residue of a removed full stop and is ALWAYS a boundary. This is the dominant signal here and alone yields about twenty-five cuts. (2) A fronted PP or temporal frame attaches FORWARD; the cut goes before it, not after it (fi al-sabah, 'ala al-janib al-akhar, fi al-fina' al-muqabil, fi al-sa'a al-thaniya wa-al-nisf, 'indaha, al-an, wa-fi al-khalf, wa-bi-su'uba, wa-ba'd ilqa' nazra). (3) waw cuts when what follows brings an overt NEW SUBJECT NP, a NEW TIME OR PLACE FRAME, or a REPEATED rhetorical frame; waw does NOT cut when the following verb is a bare continuation agreeing with the subject just named, nor when it merely joins nouns or adjectives. (4) fa- and thumma- resumptive openers that advance the action cut (fa-tahjubu, fa-ta'khudhu, fa-ashghalu, fa-yantasibu, thumma yaquduhu). (5) A subordinate clause or relative that FOLLOWS its main clause belongs to it: never cut before alladhi/allati, li-anna, hatta, baynama, ba'd, kay, or a hal depictive (wa-qawa'imuhu muqayyada, wa-nahnu nahtasi, musta'inan bi-'asa). (6) In the colophon every reconstructed abbreviation dot is a boundary (daal + dot gives a cut after daal), but a label-plus-name credit line stays whole (section A3). (7) A medial comma-set or dash-set parenthetical takes boundaries at BOTH its edges (section B5); a short trailing tail does not (B4). (8) A bare interjection is its own segment (section H3). Governing prior throughout: LAW 0 - I under-cut about 5 to 1, so at a coin-flip joint I cut.
reasoning: REGISTER CALL FIRST. The trap was to file this under section H (first-person literary memoir, 20-35 tokens, the one register where LAW 1 and LAW 2 invert and waw/fa weld). I rejected that. Section H was doc_0a957c052364, an Arabic-authored confessional voice that runs on with commas. This is a translated German diary and the gold reconstructs the Arabic translation's ink. The surface confirms it: paragraph after paragraph consists of finite clauses simply abutting with no connective at all (ya'buru bi sahra' sina' | la adri ma alladhi yantaziruni | arani mudtariban; banahu bi-nafsihi | kuntu a'taqidu; wa-al-anf | tanzi'u al-khimar | wajhuha jamil; gha'iratan | najlisu; al-qarya | yabsutu lafi). That asyndeton is the residue of removed full stops. Target set near 9-12 tokens; final answer is 76 boundaries, about 8.7 body tokens per sentence. @9 (daal). Doctrine A1/A2 and checklist item 3. 'tarjama d. Dana Shaker' - the abbreviation dot after daal is exactly the 'Robert L. Rothstein' and 'sad.ba' case that cost me five free boundaries in batch 1. Cut after daal. But A3 keeps a credit line otherwise whole, and its gold ('al-katib Muhammad Abu Qamar ||') shows a label-plus-name colon does NOT split, so 'muraja'a Mustafa al-Sulaiman' stays whole and I do not split tarjama from daal. @20 (Nuweiba). A place/region pair on a header line. A3 argues one segment; section K3 (caption subject NP splits from predicate NP) plus the comma argue two. Coin flip, so LAW 0 says cut. Marked lo. @23-27 and @567-571 (the two datelines). I did NOT split '23 Kanun al-Awwal | Disembir 2005'. Disembir is a parenthetical or slash gloss on Kanun al-Awwal, and parentheses and slashes have no boundary support anywhere in my doctrine, unlike dots and colons. Both datelines treated identically for consistency. @44 vs @47 (la bal harran). I considered cutting after dafi'an and letting 'la bal harran' stand as an appositive self-correction under LAW 3. Rejected: LAW 3 is about ASYNDETIC repetition and 'bal' is an overt connective; B4 (a short adversative clause of 3-6 tokens is a tail glued to the preceding sentence, four documented false cuts) governs. Cut at 47 only. @63 (fa-yashu al-jaww wa-yufsihu al-majal). The hardest recurring shape in this document, and the one where I refined LAW 1. LAW 1's literal test (does a new argument appear after waw?) says cut: al-majal and amam shamsin mutawahhija are new. I did NOT cut, and I applied the same reading at 346 (wa-natakki'u 'ala huzam battaniyyat) and 374 (wa-yatlu salawatihi bi-samt). The discriminator I extracted from LAW 1's own examples: its CUTTING cases either introduce an overt new subject (wa-al-fa'ida al-ra'isiyya, wa-'asimatuha Abu Zabi, wa-tashmalu shakhsiyyat) or repeat a frame (yumkinu an ... wa-yumkinu an ...); its EXEMPT cases (wa-zara'aha, wa-akala khubzan wa-shariba ma'an) are bare continuation verbs agreeing with the subject just named. yufsihu agrees with al-jaww named one token earlier; natakki'u and yatlu likewise continue subjects named inside the same clause and bring no new time or place frame. Hendiadys, not new sentences. By the same discriminator I DID cut at 211 (wa-yastahibuni bi-sayyaratihi ba'd al-zuhr) because that waw brings a new TIME frame plus a whole purpose clause, a new discourse step, and at 537 (wa-tatalabbadu al-sama') because al-sama' is an overt new subject NP. @99-121 (the fish). The ba-headed attributive list (bi-fam hayawan muftaris wa-zahr mashdud wa-za'nifat dhayl marfu'a wa-khayashim tatadalla min al-batn) runs 23 tokens with no cut, well over target, which LAW 6 flags. I left it whole on LAW 1's noun/adjective exemption plus one piece of positive evidence: every member is introduced by an overt waw, which means the Arabic used waw rather than commas, so there is no removed comma to reconstruct. That same argument spared gharghara fawwara murtajifa (@257-260) and the symptom list su'al wa-zukam wa-alam hanjara wa-qush'arira wa-alam 'adali (@543-549). @135 (wa-'indama u'idu al-nazar). Section B3 records wa-'indama as a FALSE CUT (doc_3f6c5f1e305a @540). I cut anyway. @540 sat inside section B's long expository register, whereas here wa-'indama fronts its own main clause (la ajidu) and closes the third beat of an explicit triptych (clouds cover, a fish appears; soon, a skeleton; look again, only lines). The closer precedent is section H2 @393, waw plus fronted kullama plus new main clause, which the gold cut. Marked med. @188 ('indama tatalakka' bi-al-qafz fi al-ma'). Did NOT cut. LAW 4. The test: if 'indama were fronting, its main clause would have to be hatta yadfa'una ahaduhum, but hatta is itself a subordinator, so 'indama can only TRAIL kunna nash'uru biha sighara. This is the doc_56781db1019f @634/@642 error from batch 1 in mirror image, and LAW 4 resolves it cleanly. @202 and @207 (wa-huwa shabb nahil ismuhu Lafi). A medial parenthetical separating yatakallamu from its object al-qalil al-qalil min al-injliziyya. In printed Arabic this is near-obligatorily comma-set, and B5 (doc_3f6c5f1e305a @892: 'wa-ma nahtaju kullana || afradan wa-duwalan wa-mu'assasat duwaliyya ila al-qiyam bihi') is the one documented instance of exactly this structural POSITION and it produced boundaries. Every counter-case in my doctrine that welds comma-set material (B4, K5 wa-huna, I2 wa-idha) is a TRAILING tail, not a medial interrupter, which is a real structural difference. Cut both edges: 202 med, 207 lo, since they stand or fall together. @248 (fa-yantasibu) but NOT @249 (thumma yusraju). LAW 2 says fa opening a new narrative step cuts; E2 says a bare VP chain rides along. Discriminator: the subject FLIPS at fa-yantasibu (Lafi and Rahman untie, then the camel stands up), so it is a new step; but fa-yantasibu thumma yusraju keeps one subject across two bare verbs, exactly doc_54f919517225 @1083 (wa-hafara hufra qablaha thumma dara hawlaha) which stayed one segment. The same logic gave the cut at @281 before thumma yaquduhu, where thumma carries a seven-token new goal PP, matching section E's cutting thumma (thumma ashara bi-yadihi, thumma waqafa yantaziru). @260 (wa-ka'anna ghadaban qadiman yahtashidu hunak). Genuinely 50/50 and my T2 tension in miniature. B4 says a short comma-set tail (5 tokens) welds; C4 says waw plus a new topic NP with a predicate cuts. I cut, on LAW 0's tiebreak and because ghadaban qadiman is an overt new subject introducing an independent image rather than continuing the same assertion the way B4's adversative tails do. Marked lo; logged as a T2 test case. @239 (wa-qawa'imuhu muqayyada). The mirror site, decided the OTHER way: no cut. This is a hal depictive on jamal ('kneels on its side, its legs bound'), only two tokens, and LAW 4 covers subordinate material following its main clause. Same treatment for wa-nahnu nahtasi (@350) and musta'inan bi-'asa bi-yadihi (@279). I record that 239 and 260 are decided in opposite directions on similar surfaces; my split is overt-new-subject-with-independent-predication versus adverbial depictive, and the grader's verdict on this pair is the single most informative thing I can get from this document. @293 (hadha Thuban jamaluka). Did NOT split the apposition jamaluka. G2 says an appositive inside a quote cuts, but G1 (a whole quoted utterance welds to its speech verb) cost me five false cuts in batch 1 and the quote here is only three tokens. G1 wins on weight. @330 vs @333 (wajhuha jamil fihi ba'd al-buthur wa-laha 'aynan gha'iratan). No cut at 330: fihi ba'd al-buthur is not parallel in SHAPE to wajhuha jamil, and LAW 3's discriminator is repetition, not mere continuation. Cut at 333: wa-laha 'aynan gha'iratan has an overt new subject NP with its own predicate (C4), and C2 licenses a three-token waw-clause standing alone (wa-huwa batil ||). Marked lo. @385 (lakin yufadu ilayya bi-anna dhalika laysa daruriyyan). Did NOT cut. Six tokens, right at B4's threshold, inside a nine-token paragraph; B4 has four supporting instances and this is its exact shape. Logged as a T2 test case. @405 and @407 (ahaduhum Mubarak al-dalil al-akhar). A verbless appositive block after a complete verbal sentence. 405, the asyndetic juncture between yadkhulu rijal ila al-manzil thalath marrat and the nominal block, is well supported. 407 is a positional GUESS: there is certainly a comma somewhere inside ahaduhum Mubarak al-dalil al-akhar, and 'ahaduhum Mubarak | al-dalil al-akhar' leaves both halves complete, whereas 'ahaduhum Mubarak al-dalil | al-akhar' leaves al-akhar dangling. Under LAW 0's 5:1 cost, guessing the site beats abstaining: a wrong guess costs one false cut plus one miss, abstaining costs one miss outright. Marked lo. @422 ('ajaban). A bare exclamative accusative that cannot attach syntactically to either neighbour; section H3 says a one-word turn whose exclamation or question mark was removed is its own segment. Boundaries at both 421 and 422. @466 and @473 (ana al-rajul la ushahidu mir'a fi al-manzil). Without these, 'hal dhu'irat ... am annaha turidu ... 'ala al-suwar' is a single 28-token segment, more than twice target, which LAW 6 flags as almost certainly hiding a boundary. The parenthetical is an authorial aside interrupting a hal...am question, dash-set in the original, and its two edges are the only viable joints. Both med. I resisted the further temptation to split ana | al-rajul. @492 (wa-kam yurbikuni). Only two tokens, so B4 pressure to weld. I cut, following section H2 @584-589, where the gold gave 'wa-liman asuquhu', a three-token waw-initial parallel question, its own segment. This is a REPEATED rhetorical frame (kam ... wa-kam ...), which is LAW 3's parallelism criterion operating through an overt waw. @529 (sur'ana ma tatahayya'u li-istiqbal ashkal ukhra). LAW 4 protects trailing relatives and I nearly left it. What overrode that is LAW 6: 508-535 is 28 tokens with no other viable joint, since ta'sifu and taj'alu are both relatives, fi zawba'a is an argument of ta'sifu, and the fronted PPs cannot be severed from their verb. Note the parallel with @122, where wa-sur'ana ma opened a new sentence. Marked lo. @576, @579, @588, @592, @598 (the loading of the camels). laqad usrijat al-jimal al-thalatha is a complete clause; ghita' 'ala al-sanam / 'alayhi al-sarj al-khashabi al-thaqil / wa-'ala al-sarj aghtiya wa-hasa'ir are three PARALLEL verbless locative predications, a colon followed by a list in the original, and LAW 3's parallelism plus the colon rule (A4, J1) both cut. @598 is the same shape one level down: bi-al-mu'una li-sittat ayyam, then the ba-list naming what the provisions are; marked lo because the Arabic may have stacked the two ba-phrases with no mark at all. WHAT I DELIBERATELY LEFT UNCUT, against LAW 0 pressure, and why: @77/@80 (the stacked fronted PPs 'ala al-janib al-akhar min al-khalij / fi al-sharq al-muhadhi), @306 (bila abwab wa-nawafidh matliyya), @341 ('ala ard ihda al-ghuraf / 'ala hasa'ir majdula), @510 (fi tariq al-'awda / fi 'arabat al-bik ab), @552 (ya tura). Each is a plausible comma site. But B5's licence is for parentheticals that INTERRUPT a clause, not for stacked adverbials, noun coordination, or a bound modal particle, and cutting all five would push the body below 8 tokens per sentence, denser than anything in this text supports. I log them explicitly so a grader's verdict is informative in either direction: if these five come back as misses, then my no-comma-under-waw and stacked-adverbial exemptions are both too broad and section B5 should be generalised to every reconstructed comma.
